title: Evaluate an expression tree
starter:
type expr =
  | Num of int
  | Add of expr * expr
  | Sub of expr * expr
  | Mul of expr * expr
  | Neg of expr

let rec eval (e : expr) : int =
  match e with
  | Num n -> n
  | _ -> 0
hints: The `| _ -> 0` line is the catch-all trap from this page. Delete it, and the compiler tells you which cases are missing.
Each case calls `eval` on its parts and combines the answers: `Add (a, b) -> eval a + eval b`.
`Sub (a, b)` is `a - b`, in that order. `Neg a` is minus the value of `a`, written `-(eval a)`.

answer.code:
type expr =
  | Num of int
  | Add of expr * expr
  | Sub of expr * expr
  | Mul of expr * expr
  | Neg of expr

let rec eval (e : expr) : int =
  match e with
  | Num n -> n
  | Add (a, b) -> eval a + eval b
  | Sub (a, b) -> eval a - eval b
  | Mul (a, b) -> eval a * eval b
  | Neg a -> -(eval a)
answer.explain: The reference has one case per constructor and no catch-all: `Num n -> n`, `Add (a, b) -> eval a + eval b`, `Sub (a, b) -> eval a - eval b`, `Mul (a, b) -> eval a * eval b`, `Neg a -> -(eval a)`. With every case written out, adding a sixth constructor later makes the compiler point at this function.
